paragraphs: CNO is a holding company for a group of insurance companies that develop, market and administer health insurance, annuity, individual life insurance and other insurance and financial services products. The terms "CNO Financial Group, Inc.", "CNO", the "Company", "we", "us", and "our" as used in this report refer to CNO and its subsidiaries. Such terms, when used to describe insurance business and products, refer to the insurance business and products of CNO's insurance subsidiaries.

We focus on serving middle-income pre-retiree and retired Americans, which we believe are attractive, underserved, high growth markets. We sell our products through exclusive agents, independent producers (some of whom sell one or more of our product lines exclusively) and direct marketing. As of December 31, 2025, we had total assets of $38.8 billion and shareholders' equity of $2.6 billion (which included an accumulated other comprehensive loss of $1.1 billion). For the year ended December 31, 2025, we had revenues of $4.5 billion and net income of $229.3 million. See our consolidated financial statements and accompanying footnotes for additional financial information about the Company and its segments.

We view our operations as three insurance product lines (annuity, health and life) and the investment and fee income segments. Our segments are aligned based on their common characteristics, comparability of profit margins and the way the chief operating decision maker ("CODM") makes operating decisions and assesses the performance of the business. Our CODM is the Chief Executive Officer.

We market our products through the Consumer and Worksite Divisions that reflect the customers served by the Company. The Consumer and Worksite Divisions are primarily focused on marketing insurance products, several types of which are sold in both divisions and underwritten in the same manner. The Consumer Division serves individual consumers, engaging with them on the phone, virtually, online, face-to-face with agents, or through a combination of sales channels. The structure unifies consumer capabilities into a single division and integrates the strength of our agent sales forces with one of the largest direct-to-consumer insurance businesses with proven experience in advertising, web/digital and call center support. The Worksite Division focuses on the sale of voluntary insurance benefits, including supplemental health and life insurance products in the workplace for businesses, associations, and other membership groups, interacting with customers at their place of employment and virtually.

We centralize certain functional areas, including marketing, business unit finance and sales support, among others. We primarily market our insurance products under our three primary brands: Bankers Life, Washington National and Colonial Penn.

Our executive offices are located at 11299 Illinois Street, Carmel, Indiana 46032, and our telephone number is (317) 817-6100. Our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K and amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act are available free of charge on our website at www.CNOinc.com as soon as reasonably practicable after they are electronically filed with, or furnished to, the SEC. These filings are also available on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov. Copies of these filings are also available, without charge, from CNO Investor Relations, 11299 Illinois Street, Carmel, IN 46032. Except for the documents specifically incorporated by reference into this Annual Report on Form 10-K, information contained on our website or that can be accessed through our website is not incorporated by reference in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Reference to our website is made as an inactive textual reference.

Our website also includes the charters of our Audit and Enterprise Risk Committee, Executive Committee, Governance and Nominating Committee, Human Resources and Compensation Committee and Investment Committee, as well as our Corporate Governance Guidelines and our Code of Conduct that applies to all officers, directors and employees. Copies of these documents are available free of charge on our website at www.CNOinc.com or from CNO Investor Relations at the address shown above. Within the time period specified by the SEC and the New York Stock Exchange, we will post on our website any amendment to our Code of Conduct and any waiver applicable to our principal executive officer, principal financial officer or principal accounting officer.

In May 2025, we filed with the New York Stock Exchange the Annual CEO Certification regarding the Company's compliance with their Corporate Governance listing standards as required by Section 303A.12(a) of the New York Stock Exchange Listed Company Manual. In addition, we have filed as exhibits to this 2025 Form 10-K the applicable certifications of the Company's Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer required under Section 302 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 regarding the Company's public disclosures.

CNO became the successor to Conseco, Inc., an Indiana corporation (our "Predecessor"), in connection with a bankruptcy reorganization, which became effective on September 10, 2003. Our Predecessor was organized in 1979 and commenced operations in 1982.
Data in Item 1. are provided as of or for the year ended December 31, 2025 (as the context implies), unless otherwise indicated.

Our insurance subsidiaries develop, market and administer health insurance, annuity, individual life insurance and other insurance and financial services products. We sell these products through exclusive agents, independent producers (some of whom sell one or more of our product lines exclusively) and direct marketing. We had premium collections of $4.6 billion, $4.4 billion and $4.1 billion in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Our insurance subsidiaries collectively hold licenses to market our insurance products in all fifty states, the District of Columbia, and certain protectorates of the United States. Sales to residents of the following states accounted for at least 5 percent of our 2025 collected premiums: Florida (12 percent), Iowa (6 percent), Texas (6 percent), California (5 percent), and Pennsylvania (5 percent).

We believe that most purchases of life insurance, accident and health insurance and annuity products occur only after individuals are contacted and solicited by an insurance agent. Accordingly, the success of our distribution system is largely dependent on our ability to attract and retain experienced and highly motivated agents.
We market our products through our two sales organization divisions – the Consumer and Worksite Divisions that reflect the customers served by the Company.

headings: Economic Conditions, Market Conditions and Investments:
There are risks to our business associated with broad economic conditions.
Inflation levels could have adverse consequences for us, the insurance industry and the U.S. economy
A return to a prolonged low interest rate environment may negatively impact our results of operations, financial position and cash flows.
Our investment portfolio is subject to several risks that may diminish the value of our invested assets and negatively impact our profitability, our financial condition and our liquidity.
The determination of the allowance for credit losses related to our investments is highly subjective and could have a material adverse effect on our operating results and financial condition.
Insurance Risk:
The results of operations of our insurance business will decline if our premium rates are not adequate or if we are unable to increase rates.
Our liabilities for insurance products may prove to be inadequate, requiring us to increase liabilities which results in reduced net income and shareholders' equity.
Our operating results may suffer if policyholder surrender levels differ significantly from our assumptions.
We face risk with respect to our reinsurance agreements.
Liquidity Risk:
CNO is a holding company and its liquidity and ability to meet its obligations may be constrained by the ability of CNO's insurance subsidiaries to distribute cash to it.

A decline in our current credit ratings may adversely affect our ability to access capital and the cost of such capital, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
Taxation, Laws and Regulation:
Our ability to use our existing NOLs may be limited by certain transactions, and an impairment of existing NOLs could result in a significant writedown in the value of our deferred tax assets.
Changes in tax laws could increase our tax costs and reduce sales of our insurance and annuity products.
Litigation and regulatory investigations are inherent in our business, may harm our financial condition and reputation, and may negatively impact our financial results.
Federal and state legislation could adversely affect the financial performance of our insurance operations.
Our insurance subsidiaries may be required to pay assessments to fund other companies' policyholder losses or liabilities and this may negatively impact our financial results.
General Business Risk:
Managing operational risks may not be effective in mitigating risk and loss to us.
Major public health issues could have an adverse impact on our financial condition, results of operations, liquidity, cash flows and other aspects of our business.
The occurrence of natural or man-made disasters or climate change could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
paragraphs: CNO and its businesses are subject to a number of risks including general business and financial risks. Any or all of such risks could have a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition or results of operations of CNO. In addition, please refer to the "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" section of this Form 10-K.

General factors such as the availability of credit, consumer spending, business investment, capital market conditions and inflation affect our business. Threats facing the U.S. economy include the imposition of tariffs, increasing the federal debt limit and other federal budget and taxation questions. Failure to resolve these political issues in a timely manner could result in federal government shutdowns, a default on government debt, increased costs, market disruption and volatility and impact government spending and economic activity. In an economic downturn, higher unemployment, lower family income and savings, lower corporate earnings, lower business investment and lower consumer spending may depress the demand for life insurance, annuities and other insurance products. In addition, this type of economic environment may result in higher lapses or surrenders of policies and may negatively impact the value of our assets.

Our business is exposed to the performance of the debt and equity markets. Adverse market conditions can affect the liquidity and value of our investments. The manner in which debt and equity market performance and changes in interest rates have affected, and will continue to affect, our business, financial condition, growth and profitability include, but are not limited to, the following:

•The value of our investment portfolio has been materially affected in the past by changes in market conditions which resulted in substantial realized and/or unrealized losses. Future adverse capital market conditions could result in additional realized and/or unrealized losses.

•Changes in interest rates also affect our investment portfolio. In periods of increasing interest rates, life insurance policy loans, surrenders and withdrawals could increase as policyholders seek higher returns. This could require us to sell invested assets at a time when their prices may be depressed by the increase in interest rates, which could cause us to realize investment losses. Conversely, during periods of declining interest rates, we could experience increased premium payments on products with flexible premium features, repayment of policy loans and increased percentages of policies remaining inforce. We could obtain lower returns on investments made with these cash flows. In addition, prepayment rates on investments may increase so that we might have to reinvest those proceeds in lower-yielding investments. As a consequence of these factors, we could experience a decrease in the spread between the returns on our investment portfolio and amounts to be credited to policyholders and contract holders, which could adversely affect our profitability.

•The attractiveness of some of our insurance products may decrease because they are linked to the equity markets and/or assessments of our financial strength, resulting in lower profits. Increasing consumer concerns about the returns and features of our insurance products or our financial strength may cause existing customers to surrender policies or withdraw assets, and diminish our ability to sell policies and attract assets from new and existing customers, which would result in lower sales and fee revenues.

paragraphs: Operating return on equity ("operating ROE") (a non-GAAP measure) is equal to the trailing four quarters of net operating income divided by average shareholders' equity, excluding accumulated other comprehensive loss and net operating loss carryforwards. Our operating ROE, excluding significant items, was 11.4 percent, 11.4 percent, and 8.6 percent for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. We continue to target an improvement in run‑rate operating ROE of 200 basis points through 2027, off a 2024 run-rate of approximately 10 percent.

paragraphs: CNO 是一家保險公司的控股公司，開發、行銷與管理健康保險、年金、個人壽險及其他保險與財務服務產品。本報告中所使用的 "CNO Financial Group, Inc.", "CNO", "本公司", "我們", "我們" 及 "我們的" 皆指 CNO 及其子公司。當這些詞語用來描述保險業務與產品時，則指 CNO 保險子公司的保險業務與產品。
我們將業務視為三個保險產品線（年金、健康與壽險）及投資與費用收入分部。我們的分部是根據其共同特徵、利潤率的可比性以及首席營運決策者（"CODM"）如何做出營運決策及評估業務表現而設立。我們的 CODM 是首席執行長。

我們透過消費者與工作場所分部來行銷產品，這些分部反映本公司所服務的客戶。消費者與工作場所分部主要專注於行銷保險產品，其中一些產品類型在兩個分部皆有銷售，且以相同方式承保。消費者分部服務個人客戶，透過電話、視訊、線上、面對面經理或銷售通路組合與客戶互動。此結構將消費者能力整合為一個分部，並結合我們經理銷售團隊的強項與其中一間規模最大的直接對消費者保險業務，該業務在廣告、網站/數位及客服中心支援方面有豐富經驗。工作場所分部專注於銷售自願性保險福利，包括在企業、協會及其他會員團體的工作場所中提供的補充健康與壽險產品，與客戶在工作場所及視訊上互動。
我們將某些功能部門集中管理，包括行銷、業務單位財務及銷售支援等。我們主要透過三個主要品牌來行銷保險產品：Bankers Life、Washington National 及 Colonial Penn。

本公司總部位於印第安那州卡梅爾市伊利諾伊街 11299 號，電話為 (317) 817-6100。本公司依照證券交易法第 13(a) 或 15(d) 節規定所提交的年度申報書（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）、現況申報書（Form 8-K）及這些申報書的更正文件，均會在向美國證券交易委員會（SEC） electronically filed 之後，盡速於本公司網站 www.CNOinc.com 免費提供閱覽。這些申報書亦可在 SEC 網站 www.sec.gov 查閱。這些申報書的副本亦可免費索取，請寄至 CNO 投資者關係部門，地址為印第安那州卡梅爾市伊利諾伊街 11299 號 46032。除本年度 Form 10-K 申報書中明確引用的文件外，本網站或可透過本網站存取的資訊，並未被引用為本年度 Form 10-K 申報書的一部分。本網站的參考僅作為文字參考。

本公司網站亦包含我們審計與企業風險委員會、執行委員會、治理與提名委員會、人力資源與薪酬委員會及投資委員會的委員會章程，以及我們的公司治理指引與適用於所有高層管理人員、董事及員工的行為準則。這些文件的副本可免費在本公司網站 www.CNOinc.com 取得，或從 CNO 投資者關係部門地址取得。在 SEC 及紐約證券交易所規定的時間內，我們將在網站上張貼我們行為準則的任何修正案，以及適用於我們首席執行長、首席財務長或首席會計長的任何豁免事項。
2025 年 5 月，我們向紐約證券交易所提交了年度首席執行長認證，以說明本公司是否符合其公司治理上市標準，如紐約證券交易所上市公司手冊第 303A.12(a) 章節所要求。此外，我們亦在本年度 Form 10-K 中提交了適用於本公司首席執行長及首席財務長的認證，以符合 2002 年薩班斯-奧克斯利法案第 302 章節對本公司公開披露的規定。
CNO 成為 Conseco, Inc. 的繼承者，Conseco, Inc. 為一間印第安納州公司（我們的 "前公司"），此繼承關係係因破產重整而產生，該重整於 2003 年 9 月 10 日生效。我們的前公司於 1979 年設立，並於 1982 年開始營運。
第 1 項所載資料係截至或針對 2025 年 12 月 31 日終結之會計年度（除非另有說明，否則均以此為背景）。
我們的保險子公司 collectively 持有在美國五十州、華盛頓特區及美國某些保護領地銷售我們保險產品之許可證。銷售給以下州的居民，佔我們 2025 年所收保費至少 5%：佛羅裏達州（12%）、愛荷華州（6%）、德克薩斯州（6%）、加州（5%）及賓州（5%）。
我們認為，大多數壽險、意外與健康保險及年金產品之購買行為，僅發生在個人被保險經理接觸並勸募之後。因此，我們銷售系統的成功 largely 取決於我們吸引並留住經驗豐富且高度動機之保險經理之能力。
我們透過我們的兩個銷售組織部門行銷我們的產品 – 消費者部門與工作場所部門，這些部門反映本公司所服務的客戶。

headings: 經濟情勢、市場情勢及投資：
我們的業務與廣泛的經濟情勢有關聯，存在相關風險。
通貨膨脹水平可能對我們、保險業及美國經濟產生不利影響。
若出現長時間低利率環境，可能對我們的營運結果、財務狀況及現金流產生負面影響。
我們的投資組合面臨多種風險，這些風險可能降低我們投資資產的價值，並對我們的獲利能力、財務狀況及流動性產生負面影響。
有關我們投資的信用減損準備金的決定具有高度主觀性，可能對我們的營運結果及財務狀況產生重大不利影響。
保險風險：
若我們的保費率不足或無法提高保費率，我們的保險業務營運結果將會下降。
本公司對於保險產品的負債可能不足，導致需提高負債，進而造成淨收入與股東權益減少。
若保單持有人解約率與本公司預期有顯著差異，可能導致營運成果受損。
本公司對於再保險協議面臨風險。
流動性風險：
CNO 為一控股公司，其流動性及履行義務的能力可能受其保險子公司能否將現金轉撥至 CNO 之限制。
本公司現行信用評級若下降，可能不利於取得資金及資金成本，進而對財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。
稅務、法律與法規：
本公司使用現有納稅虧損（NOLs）的能力可能因某些交易而受到限制，且現有納稅虧損若發生減損，可能導致遞延稅資產價值產生重大減記。
稅法變更可能增加我們的稅務成本，並降低我們保險及年金產品的銷售額。
訴訟及監管調查是我們業務的一部分，可能損害我們的財務狀況與聲譽，並可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
聯邦及州級立法可能不利於我們保險業務的財務表現。
我們的保險子公司可能被要求支付費用以彌補其他公司保單持有人的損失或負債，這可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
一般業務風險：
管理運營風險可能無法有效降低我們的風險與損失。
重大公共衛生問題可能對我們的財務狀況、營運結果、流動性、現金流及其他業務方面產生不利影響。
自然或人為災難或氣候變遷的發生可能對我們的財務狀況與營運結果產生不利影響。
paragraphs: CNO 及其業務面臨許多風險，包括一般商業與財務風險。任何或全部這些風險都可能對 CNO 的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。此外，請參閱本 Form 10-K 的『關於未來展望陳述的警示聲明』部分。

一般因素，如信貸可得性、消費者支出、企業投資、資本市場狀況及通貨膨脹，會影響我們的業務。美國經濟面臨的威脅包括課徵關稅、提高聯邦債務上限及其他聯邦預算與稅收問題。未能及時解決這些政治問題，可能會導致聯邦政府停擺、政府債務違約、成本增加、市場動盪與波動，並影響政府支出與經濟活動。在經濟衰退期間，較高的失業率、較低的家庭收入與儲蓄、較低的企業獲利、較低的企業投資與較低的消費者支出，可能會壓抑壽險、年金及其他保險產品的需求。此外，這種經濟環境可能會導致保單解約或贖回率提高，並可能對我們資產的價值產生負面影響。
我們的業務會受到債務與股權市場表現的影響。不利的市場條件會影響我們投資的流動性與價值。債務與股權市場表現及利率變動如何影響，以及將持續影響我們的業務、財務狀況、成長與獲利能力，包括但不限於以下各項：
• 我們投資組合的價值過去曾因市場條件變動而受到重大影響，導致實現與/或未實現損失。未來不利的資本市場條件可能會導致額外的實現與/或未實現損失。

• 利率變動也會影響我們的投資組合。在利率上升期間，保單持有人可能因追求更高回報而增加壽險保單貸款、贖回與提領，這可能會導致我們在利率上升時出售投資資產，而當時這些資產的價格可能因利率上升而下跌，造成我們實現投資損失。相反地，在利率下降期間，我們可能會因具有彈性 Premium 特徵的產品而面臨更高的 Premium 支付、保單貸款償還以及保單持續有效率提高。我們可能從這些現金流中獲得較低的投資回報。此外，投資的預付率可能上升，使得我們必須將這些資金重新投資於收益率較低的投資項目。由於這些因素，我們可能會面臨投資組合回報與應計給保單持有人及契約持有人金額之間的利差減少，這可能會對我們的獲利能力產生不利影響。
• 一些我們的保險產品可能因與股權市場連結或對我們財務強度的評估而變得較不具吸引力，導致較低的獲利。消費者對我們保險產品的回報與功能或我們財務強度的擔憂，可能會導致現有客戶贖回保單或提領資產，並削弱我們銷售保單與吸引新舊客戶資金的能力，這將導致銷售與費用收入減少。
